Subject: Private deployment: BYOK evidence, subprocessors, and transfers

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Our security team had a few follow-ups specific to the planned on-prem / VPC deployment:

- We need a short evidence packet showing how Redwood implements BYOK for private deployments (key custody, rotation windows, and operator access model).
- Canonical list of current subprocessors (including any cloud infra and regional partners) and their roles.
- Clarification on cross-border data transfers and whether any subprocessors process data outside the US when deployed in our VPC.

Can you confirm what you can share today and an expected delivery timeline? Our auditors are looking for materials by next Tuesday.

Best,
Jack

MediCorp

Jack —

Appreciate the follow-ups and the clear list. We can provide a consolidated packet that covers BYOK mechanics, operator access boundaries, and a stamped subprocessor roster.

Quick notes:
- I'll attach a concise BYOK evidence summary and the current subprocessor CSV (redacted where appropriate).
- Cross-border processing: for Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments we route telemetry and control-plane signals per the customer-selected region. We will enumerate any partner endpoints that receive operational metadata.
- Where customers require full custody (no Redwood access), we offer a BYOK-only mode + optional escrow for emergency recovery; we will flag which options are covered in the DPA addendum.

I've looped in Karthik for the technical mapping and Marissa to confirm legal/offer language. Expect an initial packet from me by EOD today and a finalized DocuSign addendum by Tuesday if that works.

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-05-04T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: BYOK evidence, subprocessors, and transfers

Soojin / Marissa —

Technical point list for the packet (to include in BYOK-Evidence-Summary):

1) Key lifecycle: Customer generates CMK in their KMS and provides the public key to Redwood. Private deploy runtime stores only key references; decryption operations (when required) are performed in-customer KMS or via a hardware-isolated proxy in their VPC.
2) Operator access: Minimal privileged Op roles exist for bootstrapping and emergency breakglass; all actions are logged and require two-person authorization. We can supply an operator access matrix and sample audit extract.
3) Telemetry: Application-level telemetry (API health, queue depth, perf metrics) can be routed to Redwood telemetry endpoints or forwarded to a customer endpoint; PII is not included by default. We'll list exact attributes forwarded.
4) Escrow options: We currently support (a) no-escrow (customer sole custody), (b) encrypted escrow with customer-wrapped keys, (c) sealed-escrow with HSM-backed retrieval under legal process.

I attached the runbook extract that maps operator capabilities to the telemetry/keys table (privdep-runbook-v1.2.md).

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer — Private Deployments
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Thanks — this looks good. A few commercial/legal asks before we send externally:

- Confirm whether the DPA addendum will include a clause explicitly stating that Redwood will not access customer plaintext when BYOK-only mode is selected (we should add standard wording and an audit sample).
- For subprocessors: provide a short description column covering purpose + country of processing. Redact contact emails if necessary.
- Pricing/ops: if customer wants sealed-escrow with HSM retrieval, this is an add-on. Please mark that in the packet and give an estimate.

Soojin: once Karthik confirms the final runbook snippet and we have the subprocessor descriptions, loop Legal (I can intro to our contracts counsel) and send to Jack with a proposed DocuSign addendum.

Marissa Cole

Jack —

Attached is the consolidated packet and answers to your auditor bullets. Highlights:

- Operator breakglass: included a redacted sample of a two-person auth log and an overview of the approval chain (we control via RBAC + signed audit events).
- Subprocessors: section added with name / country / purpose / SCC status for each partner (see subprocessor-list-2025.csv). Any partner that may process op-metadata outside the US is explicitly flagged.
- Sealed-escrow retrieval: by default we require a court-ordered retrieval path for sealed-escrow HSM releases; we also offer a trustee-based retrieval design but that requires additional onboarding and an escrow agreement (commercial add-on).
